title: Per-tenant commitment fabric and soft-decline proxy for dedicated fleets
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem: Dedicated fleets must provide predictable committed throughput for tenant contracts while avoiding catastrophic failure modes during short-lived spikes. Current shedding strategies are binary (accept or drop) and cause poor UX for customers that could tolerate partial progress or soft degradations. Goal: implement a per-tenant commitment fabric that tracks committed throughput (tokens/sec or rps), maintains a credit balance, emits autoscaler and routing hints, and a soft-decline proxy that returns partial progress semantics and suggested retry windows instead of hard drops. This feature should integrate with existing admission layers, expose telemetry to Console, and be pluggable per-dedicated-pool configuration.
motivation:
- Reduce customer disruptions during overload by offering graceful degradation modes (partial responses, slower rate, alternative model variants).
- Enforce contract-level guarantees while allowing short bursts via credit drawdown.
- Provide autoscaler signals and routing hints derived from committed vs observed consumption so Dedicated can proactively scale or route.
acceptance_criteria: Per-tenant commitment object exists in the admission path and is consultable via RPC (tenant id -> committed_rate, burst_credit, last_refill).
Soft-decline proxy returns 207-like partial-accept semantics with metadata: accepted_tokens, suggested_retry_after_seconds, alternative_model_variant when capacity constrained.
Credit accounting persists across requests for active sessions and drains predictably for bursts; unit tests cover edge cases (concurrent draws, lease expiry, rollover).
Autoscaler hint events emitted when usage-to-commitment ratio exceeds 85% for 3 consecutive minutes and when credit pool < 20% for 60s.

End-to-end load tests: under a mixed workload (80% baseline, 20% burst), P99 latency under soft-decline path increases by <15% and effective customer-visible error rate drops compared to hard-shed baseline.
Console dashboards surface per-tenant commit utilization, outstanding credits, and recent soft-decline incidents with links to traces.
Canary rollout in one DA (dedicated-avail) with synthetic tenant traffic proves behavior before fleet-wide enablement.
implementation_notes:
- Admission layer will consult a per-tenant in-memory commitment record with atomic decrement semantics; fallback to per-pool default when missing.
- Credit behavior: steady refill rate = committed_rate, burst buffer = min(committed_rate * burst_window, configured_max_burst). Credits can go negative up to a configured debt_limit to allow transient overruns, after which soft-decline engages.
- Soft-decline proxy strategy: if admission denies full acceptance, accept a degraded form where feasible (shorter max tokens, lower temperature, smaller model) and attach suggestion headers; otherwise return structured soft-decline response for client to retry according to suggested backoff.
- Autoscaler hooks: emit events via metrics bus and the existing fleet-hint topic with tags {tenant_id, pool, commit_util_ratio, credit_pct}.
risks_and_mitigations:
- Risk: Credit drift across restarts causing incorrect guarantees. Mitigation: persist checkpoint to local durable store and rebuild on startup; use short lived leases and conservative refill until checkpoint validated.
- Risk: Clients ignore suggested retry windows and hammer the system. Mitigation: response includes a rate-limited token and a server-enforced short-term token bucket for retries; also document SDK support for honoring soft-decline semantics.
- Risk: Increased admission path latency. Mitigation: commitment lookup is in-process cache; hot-path optimized and fallback to approximate values when cold.
rollout_plan: 1) Unit + integration tests; 2) Internal canary in staging with synthetic tenants; 3) Canary in dedicated-avail pool for 2 low-risk customers; 4) Monitor 24/7 metrics and runbook; 5) Gradual 25% to 100% enablement by tenant cohorts over two weeks.
testing_plan:
- Write deterministic simulator that replays mixed tenant traffic and verifies credit accounting and soft-decline outcomes.
- Load tests to compare hard-shed baseline vs soft-decline under identical stress traces.
- Chaos test: restart admission service to validate checkpointing and recovery.
dashboards_and_alerts: Dedicated/Admission/SoftDeclineRate (alert high rate and correlated error responses)
Autoscaler/HintsEmitted (counter of emitted scale hints per pool)
